column12: launched at 1435 with the Ryujo as its objective ... originally 30 dive bombers and 8 torpedo planes; Ryujo, a heavy cruiser and three destroyers 'bearing 317 T., distance 198 miles from our force' (Enterprise scouts, 1440)

Saratoga was about 5-8 mi from Enterprise (ONI says carriers about 5 miles apart; Cv6 report says Saratoga 10-15 mi on disengaged side later). Ryujo was steering SW at ~30 kn toward the US force (closing). Strike found Ryujo only at 1606 at 06-30S 160-45E (after chasing a second sighting 75 mi NE of Ryujo), attack began 1620, i.e. about 91 min to find it. One SBD and one TBF turned back mechanical. Groups recovered Saratoga ~1845 and after sunset; 'Not a pilot, crewman, or plane of the Saratoga attack group was lost'. Return carrier position not stated. No fuel loss.

Idea of striking Ryujo earlier was abandoned for fear planes 'would not be able to return before nightfall' (doctrine.md). 7 F4F stayed as CAP. Planes flew on 'following instructions' to Henderson Field (all but one TBF) and spent the night there: 36 landed ashore. Why ashore: ONI says only 'following instructions'; inferred reason: the convoy was a search target far from the carrier and recovery on return was not expected (not stated). Next morning the group, minus two SBD forced back to the island field, rejoined Saratoga about 1130 (deferred rendezvous 0800 -> 1100).

Report uses 'zone plus 10' clock and writes the launch time as '090'; ONI shows 0700 (different zone, not converted). OUTCOMES: no Hornet fighter returned to the ship: they stayed with the SBD until forced to head for Midway for lack of gas; 5 pilots rescued (ONI: 8). 13 SBD of Bombing 8 landed at Midway for lack of gas, 2 in the lagoon out of gas; 11 gassed and returned to Hornet 1727. Scouting 8 and Bombing 8 never found the enemy. 15 TBDs (Waldron) found it and were lost to combat.
